sections.html:
San Juan County fills the northwest corner of New Mexico, with Aztec as the county seat. Its 2020 census population was 121,661, and it is part of the Farmington metropolitan area. The Navajo Nation covers 60.45 percent of the county's area, so much of the county lies outside the ordinary city lots of Farmington, Aztec and Bloomfield.

Other communities include Kirtland, Flora Vista, Fruitland, Waterflow, Shiprock, Lee Acres, Navajo Dam and Nenahnezad. The bill depends on the school district, city and voter-approved bonds covering a property, so where the house sits changes what the owner pays. Energy, health care and education supply most of the jobs, which means demand for homes tends to follow the oil and gas cycle.

Taxable value is one third of full value, and the rate is applied to that amount. The Assessor compiles a tax roll, a county appraiser sets the full value, and the rate is stated in dollars per thousand.

The rate comes from outside the county offices. The State Department of Finance and Administration sets it every year from budgets submitted by schools, cities and voters through approved bond issues, and certifies it each September. Value changes usually come from additions to a building or from the reappraisal the Legislature requires every two years.

StepWho does itWhen
Reappraise propertyCounty AssessorEvery two years, per state mandate
Mail Notice of ValueCounty AssessorBefore April 1, usually late March

sections.h2: Due dates, late charges and where to pay
sections.html:
The first half and the full year are due on November 10, and the second half is due on April 10. Bills are released November 1. Penalty and interest begin December 11 on the first half and May 11 on the second.

The Treasurer sends a reminder on April 1 to owners with a balance from earlier years, and a delinquent notice after the second-half due date. Three or more years of back taxes can put a property on the State of New Mexico's auction list.

You can pay in any of five ways:

  • In person at the Treasurer's windows, 100 S. Oliver Dr., Suite 300, Aztec, NM 87410
  • By mail to the processing center at San Juan County Treasurer Dept. #31087, P.O. Box 27839, Albuquerque, NM 87125-7839
  • By mail to the physical address in Aztec
  • In the drop box on the east side of the County Administration building
  • Online through the county's tax portal

A valid mailing address is needed for timely delivery, and the Assessor at 505-334-6157 handles address changes. Not receiving a bill does not remove the duty to pay, late charges included.

Three programs come up most often: head of family, the veteran exemption and the value freeze for some older or disabled owners. Head of family is $2,000 off taxable value, covers residential property only, and renews on its own once claimed.

For the veteran exemption, an honorably discharged veteran living in New Mexico brings a certificate of eligibility from the county veteran service office to the Assessor in person between January 1 and April 30. A disabled veteran's occupied principal residence can be exempt in an amount equal to the federal disability percentage. The county lists that office at 1800 E. 30th St., Farmington.

The limit on value increases covers a single-family dwelling owned and occupied by someone 65 or older, or disabled, whose income stays under an inflation-adjusted limit. You must apply, and apply again each year for three years.

State law also caps residential value growth. Under Section 7-36-21.2, the value may not exceed the higher of 103 percent of the prior year or 106.1 percent of two years earlier. A change of ownership in the prior year lifts that cap for the following tax year. The state's protest pamphlet has the statute text.

Visit the Assessor first. Talk to an appraiser in person, and if you still disagree, request a protest packet. You have thirty days from the mailing date of the Notice of Value to file with the County Valuation Protest Board through the Assessor's office.

The Assessor notifies you by certified mail at least fifteen days before the hearing. State law puts the burden of proving the value wrong on the owner, so bring evidence: recent comparable sales, a repair estimate, photographs of damage or a recent appraisal.

A Notice of Value is not a tax bill. If the value, mailing address and property description are right, no action is needed.

Three things trip up sellers: the mobile home release, the river-flood paperwork and the state auction rule. A mobile home tax release is required for a duplicate title, a title change and a moving permit. The Treasurer charges $5 for a regular release and $25 for a moving permit, and takes certified funds only, with no personal or business checks.

Unpaid mobile home and personal property tax follows its own path. A Pre-Demand Warrant gives ten business days to pay or arrange payment. After that, a Demand Warrant is served by a deputy sheriff with a $42 fee for each delivery.

If your property sits near the San Juan or Animas rivers, keep damage records and insurance claim papers together, since both affect what a buyer will pay.

For real estate, the State Property Tax Division auctions long-delinquent parcels as is, with no right of redemption. Cash Home Buyers speaks with San Juan County owners who would rather close on their own timeline than wait for that.

Practical order: get the Treasurer's balance for every year, confirm the exemptions on file with the Assessor, and give both to your title company before the buyer's deadline.

faqs.q: When is San Juan County, NM property tax due?
faqs.a: The first half and full amount are due November 10, and the second half is due April 10. Penalty and interest start December 11 on the first half and May 11 on the second.

faqs.q: Where do I pay San Juan County property tax?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's office is at 100 S. Oliver Dr., Suite 300, in Aztec. You can also pay by mail, at the drop box on the east side of the administration building, or online through the county's portal.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a protest in San Juan County?
faqs.a: You have thirty days from the date the Notice of Value was mailed. File through the Assessor's office with the County Valuation Protest Board; the owner carries the burden of showing the value is wrong.

faqs.q: How much is the head of family exemption in San Juan County?
faqs.a: It is $2,000, deducted from taxable value on residential property only. After you sign up, it renews automatically each year.

faqs.q: What happens after three years of unpaid property tax in San Juan County?
faqs.a: The property can be added to the auction list kept by the State of New Mexico. Failure to pay three or more years of back taxes could lead to that.
